title: Cipher and Border
premise: Ulyana Okafor, a disgraced intelligence analyst haunted by a botched operation that cost lives, is hiding in a safe house when he finds it listed on a real estate site — interior photos, his belongings, everything. The listing is a message: someone knows exactly where he is, and they want him to come out. He traces it to Mara Voss, a cryptographer defecting from the network that destroyed his career, who claims she can prove the 'incident' was engineered. Ulyana must extract her across three countries while realizing she may be bait for the man who framed him — and that his only path home runs through trusting the ragtag team of exiles he once kept at arm's length. In the end, Ulyana chooses the found family over the institution, exposing the truth at the cost of his old identity, and finally sleeps through the night.
about_author: Emrys Whitlock is the pen name of a former logistics consultant who spent a decade moving people and cargo across borders he was never allowed to ask about. He writes thrillers about the people systems forget, from a farmhouse where the internet is optional and the coffee is not.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Insomniac and paranoid, Ulyana scrolls real estate sites as a ritual of normalcy and finds his own safe house listed with photos of his life inside. He verifies no breach occurred — the photos were taken while he slept. Emotional beat: the floor drops out; invisibility was an illusion, and someone has been watching him be human.

chapters.title: Dead Drop, Live Wire
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Following the listing's metadata to a burner contact, he receives a partial file: encrypted evidence that the incident which ended his career was staged by his own former director, Callum Reyes. The sender signs herself M.V. Emotional beat: rage curdling into purpose — for the first time in years he wants something more than sleep.

chapters.title: Mara
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins with Mara Voss, a defector hiding in Trieste who engineered the listing as the only way to reach a man with nothing left to lose. She reveals the full scope: Reyes sold the operation, and her decryption key dies with her unless she reaches extraction. Emotional beat: two broken people negotiating trust neither can afford.

chapters.title: The Team Nobody Assigned
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. To move Mara he needs help, so he calls in favors from fellow castoffs: Dov, a forger; Priya, a comms ghost; Tomas, a driver with a debt. Each refuses first, then shows up anyway. Emotional beat: reluctant warmth — the exiles assembling into something like a family, though Ulyana keeps one foot out the door.

chapters.title: Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The extraction convoy crosses into Slovenia and hits an inspection too precise to be luck — Reyes's people knew the route. Ulyana realizes there's a leak, and every eye turns inward. They improvise through on nerve alone. Emotional beat: fear bonding them tighter than trust ever could; Ulyana catches himself protecting others before himself.

chapters.title: What the Key Opens
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Safe in a mountain chapel, Mara decrypts the archive and finds not just proof against Reyes but a list of names — assets burned to protect him, including the operative whose death broke Ulyana. She hesitates to show him. Emotional beat: grief as revelation; Ulyana's insomnia reframed as mourning he never allowed himself.

chapters.title: The Bait Question
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Dov discovers the leak: the extraction route was fed to Reyes deliberately — by Mara's handler, meaning Mara may be unknowing bait to draw Ulyana into a kill box. Confronted, Mara offers to walk away rather than endanger them. Emotional beat: the family fractures over whether love requires certainty; Ulyana chooses to believe her.

chapters.title: Trieste After Dark
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Instead of running, they go on offense: a trap within the trap, using the leaked route to feed Reyes false positioning while the real team moves on his broker in Trieste. The handoff goes wrong; Dov takes a bullet shielding Mara. Emotional beat: terror and ferocity — Ulyana fights not like a survivor but like a man with people to lose.

chapters.title: Reyes
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Climax aboard a moored freighter, where Ulyana trades the decrypted archive for leverage and faces Reyes, who offers him reinstatement if he surrenders Mara. Ulyana broadcasts the evidence instead, burning his last bridge to the agency as Reyes is taken by his own masters. Emotional beat: catharsis — vengeance refused in favor of truth, and the discovery that belonging was the thing he'd been extracting all along.

chapters.title: The House That Sold Itself
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, closing. Weeks later, the team regroups at the safe house — now legally theirs, purchased with broker money Dov insists was 'found.' Ulyana fixes the porch light, hangs curtains over windows once photographed by enemies, and sleeps until morning. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — home is not a place you hide in but the people who know where to find you.
